title: Section functors and structural module maps on small ringed sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in the common module universe [def-weil-size-convention] [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For a sheaf of rings $R$ on $\mathcal C$, use the category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with its canonical small-site Grothendieck abelian structure. For $V\in\mathcal C$, define $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Ab}}(V,-):\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ by $M\mapsto M(V)$, forgetting the $R(V)$-action, and by evaluation on morphisms. For a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, ring sheaves $S$ on $\mathcal D$ and $R$ on $\mathcal C$, and a structural map $a:S\to u_*R$, use the canonical additive module direct image $M\mapsto (V\mapsto M(u(V)))$, with $S(V)$-action restricted along $a_V:S(V)\to R(u(V))$, and with sectionwise action on morphisms. When $S,R$ are commutative ring sheaves, its underlying structural map of ring sheaves is obtained by forgetting commutativity in $a$; no scalar map is chosen independently.
